title: AWS multi-region EKS · follow one request
explanation: Two regions, two VPCs, two EKS clusters. Follow a request from DNS to ALB, nodes and pods, then back. Orange: routing. Cyan: apps. Violet: control/data. Click Start journey.

steps.title: 1 / DNS chooses a region
steps.explanation: The browser asks its DNS resolver for app.example.com. Route 53 returns a healthy regional ALB endpoint using latency routing and configured health evaluation. The browser then makes HTTPS directly to that endpoint. HTTP does not pass through Route 53. Existing connections and cached DNS answers do not migrate instantly.

steps.title: 2 / Inside a regional VPC
steps.explanation: Blue frames show networking; violet frames are EC2 nodes. The ALB spans public subnets in at least two AZs; app nodes and pods sit in private subnets. The internet gateway/public routes admit internet traffic to the ALB. VPC routes, ALB/target security groups and subnet NACLs govern onward traffic. NAT is for private-subnet outbound internet access, not this inbound request path. Click a node or pod to inspect it.

objects.label: VPC 10.0.0.0/16
objects.description:

NAT is for private-subnet outbound internet access, not this inbound request path. Click a node or pod to inspect it.

A VPC is a network boundary, not an application proxy.

objects.label: Internet gateway
objects.description: The VPC internet gateway and public-subnet route tables enable internet access for the internet-facing ALB. It is a networking component, not an HTTP service.

objects.label: Regional ALB
objects.description: Logical ALB spans public subnets in AZ-a and AZ-b. ALB security group accepts HTTPS; target security groups allow the application port from the ALB.

objects.label: EC2 node / AZ-a
objects.description: An EC2 worker node runs kubelet, the container runtime and multiple pods. It is cluster-scoped.

objects.label: EC2 node / AZ-b
objects.description: A second worker node supports cross-AZ availability.

objects.label: App pod A
objects.description: Ready app pod with a routable VPC IP supplied by the Amazon VPC CNI.

steps.title: 3 / ALB selects one ready pod
steps.explanation: Chosen mode: AWS Load Balancer Controller with ALB target-type IP. Listener host/path rules choose a target group; ALB forwards the request to one healthy pod IP. A single request is not broadcast to all replicas. Packets reach the pod hosted on an EC2 node, but there is no separate NodePort/Service-IP hop in this mode. Instance target mode instead uses node NodePort and service forwarding.

steps.title: 4 / Namespaces span nodes
steps.explanation: This is a logical overlay, not physical network layering. The web namespace owns the app Pods, Service and Deployment across both nodes. The monitoring namespace also has pods on those same nodes. Nodes are cluster-scoped. Namespaces cannot be nested and do not sit inside EC2 nodes. A namespace is not a firewall: network isolation requires suitable NetworkPolicy enforcement.

objects.label: EC2 node A
objects.description:
This is a logical overlay, not physical network layering. The web namespace owns the app Pods, Service and Deployment across both nodes. The monitoring namespace also has pods on those same nodes. Nodes are cluster-scoped. Namespaces cannot be nested and do not sit inside EC2 nodes. A namespace is not a firewall: network isolation requires suitable NetworkPolicy enforcement.

Nodes belong to the cluster, not to a namespace.

objects.label: EC2 node B
objects.description: A node can host pods from several namespaces.

objects.label: Namespace: web
objects.description: Logical resource grouping, drawn as a band across nodes. It is not a subnet or request hop. Namespaces alone do not enforce network isolation.

objects.label: Namespace: monitoring
objects.description: A separate logical namespace can share the same worker nodes. Use RBAC, quotas and NetworkPolicy as appropriate.

steps.title: 5 / What configures the request path?
steps.explanation: Configuration relationships only: the Deployment maintains replicas; EKS schedules pods onto nodes. Ingress host/path rules reference a Service; its selectors and endpoint information identify app pods. The AWS Load Balancer Controller reconciles this into ALB rules and IP target groups. The control plane, Deployment, Ingress object and controller are not sequential HTTP hops.

objects.label: Managed EKS control plane
objects.description:
Configuration relationships only: the Deployment maintains replicas; EKS schedules pods onto nodes. Ingress host/path rules reference a Service; its selectors and endpoint information identify app pods. The AWS Load Balancer Controller reconciles this into ALB rules and IP target groups. The control plane, Deployment, Ingress object and controller are not sequential HTTP hops.

AWS operates the Kubernetes API server, scheduler and control-plane components in AWS-managed infrastructure. App HTTP requests do not traverse it.

objects.label: web / Deployment
objects.description: The Deployment manages ReplicaSets and desired app replicas. The scheduler places pods on eligible nodes; kubelet starts containers.

objects.label: web / Ingress
objects.description: Declarative host/path configuration referencing the web Service. This is not necessarily an ingress proxy pod.

objects.label: web / Service
objects.description: Selectors identify app pods. EndpointSlices track endpoints; readiness and ALB target health determine eligibility. Service belongs to a namespace.

objects.label: Load Balancer Controller
objects.description: Watches Kubernetes resources and reconciles ALB listeners, rules, target groups and pod-IP targets through AWS APIs. It does not proxy app requests.

steps.title: 6 / The pod calls an internal service
steps.explanation: An example app dependency: the frontend resolves api.web.svc.cluster.local using CoreDNS, then calls the API Service virtual IP. The service data plane (for example kube-proxy) forwards to one eligible API pod, possibly on another node. The API can query a database using appropriate identity and network permissions. Here a ClusterIP Service IS part of the internal routing path.

objects.label: Frontend pod
objects.description: An example app dependency: the frontend resolves api.web.svc.cluster.local using CoreDNS, then calls the API Service virtual IP. The service data plane (for example kube-proxy) forwards to one eligible API pod, possibly on another node. The API can query a database using appropriate identity and network permissions. Here a ClusterIP Service IS part of the internal routing path.

objects.label: CoreDNS
objects.description: Resolves internal Kubernetes service names. DNS lookup is separate from the HTTP request.

objects.label: api.web.svc.cluster.local
objects.description: ClusterIP Service offers a stable virtual IP. Service forwarding selects an eligible backend; it is not itself an application process.

objects.label: Database / cache
objects.description: An external managed data service is one option. Permissions, secrets, network access and application consistency must be designed explicitly.

steps.title: 7 / Response and resilience
steps.explanation: The selected pod returns the response over the established connection through the ALB to the browser. Readiness probes and ALB health checks remove unhealthy targets; Deployments replace lost pods. HPA can add pods, while node autoscaling supplies capacity. Multiple replicas across AZs improve availability, but topology spread, capacity and disruption settings must be configured. These are mechanisms, not a guarantee of zero interruption.

steps.title: 8 / A region becomes unavailable
steps.explanation: Mumbai is shown unavailable. With health evaluation configured, new DNS answers can direct clients to Virginia; cached answers and existing connections mean switchover takes time. Virginia has its own EKS cluster, VPC and ready replicas. EKS does not span regions or automatically copy deployments, sessions or databases. Recovery also requires replicated app configuration, sufficient capacity and a deliberate data/session strategy. Multi-region redundancy is different from multi-AZ redundancy.
